scientific_queries.note: Nonlinear replication of R136's exact zero, to test whether the redundancy is model-specific.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round puts the previous claim under a different model family and narrows it.

what_survives_and_what_is_narrowed.survives: the algebraic fact: each drug maps to one pathway level, so pathway one-hots are a linear transform of drug one-hots and span no new directions for a linear model
what_survives_and_what_is_narrowed.narrowed: the functional claim 'substitute, never complement' holds only for linear models; under boosting the coarsening adds +0.0152, fifteen times its minimum detectable effect
what_survives_and_what_is_narrowed.corrected: pathway carries no additional information, but its coarser granularity is a useful inductive bias for a nonlinear model

why_boosting_can_use_it.ridge: adding a linear transform of existing columns leaves the column space unchanged
why_boosting_can_use_it.boosting: the same information at a coarser granularity enables splits that generalise across all drugs in a pathway, which a split on drug identity cannot do
why_boosting_can_use_it.consequence: redundant features can still help nonlinear models; no new information does not mean no use

how_big.comparable_to: the +0.020 and +0.025 rank gains when one drug was seen (C103)
how_big.reading: small but on the same footing as the substitute effect in the partially-informed regime

limits: only thirty splits, so power is lower, though the interval is narrow
integer coding suits trees, so the ridge integer rows are references only
the boosting hyperparameters were not tuned and could change the magnitude
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: test whether the boosting gain also falls monotonically with how much identity is supplied, which would give one unified statement
